summary: Backup flow review fixes: pre-effect restore failures settle failed, restore staging is removed, retention keeps the settling point, skips undeletable points and runs outside the backup lock, interrupted publication is reconciled instead of captured again, catalog import checks capacity once, history paging survives settlements, and the member repository record is written under the backup lock. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: Operators now see restores that stop before any effect fail and release their point, published backups succeed with a note when retention skips a point, and interrupted publications fail instead of capturing again.

api.reason: Routes and payloads are unchanged. A succeeded run may carry an error naming points retention skipped; a history page generation covers record membership and order only; a Core that is no longer master answers history pages with 503 instead of 409, which the Controller already relays as 503.

roadmap.reason: Fixes review findings in the current destination acceptance slice.

state.reason: No new durable record. The publication stage and retention note live in the pool master's existing run record, which the backup authority already replicates; restore staging and capture work are host-local scratch that Core now removes.

verification.method: Focused Go regressions in internal/agent, each shown failing with its fix reverted through a go test -overlay mutant and passing after; the new tests also passed with -race. The whole internal/agent package passed.
verification.limits: No lab, remote repository or forge CI run. The single-capacity-check import, the import prune sequence and the member repository lock have no dedicated test. A point captured on a host whose clock runs ahead can still outrank later points until it ages out.
